title: Emrys and the Letters
premise: Ivo Oyelaran has spent ten years ghostwriting other people's truths, including the memoirs of his rival, celebrated novelist Marguerite Vale — while burying the one truth he never wrote down: that he and Marguerite were lovers in their twenties, and that a letter he never sent ended everything. When a snowstorm traps them together at a remote inn with the manuscript between them, Marguerite discovers her own story written in his hand, and in it, the sentence he rehearsed for a decade. As the storm traps them and the memoir's publication deadline looms, loyalty to his contract wars with the truth he owes her. At the climax, Ivo chooses truth over duty, reading the unsent letter aloud as the snow melts; Marguerite, in turn, cuts the memoir's final chapter and replaces it with a letter of her own. The book ends with them co-writing a new story — this time with both names on the cover.
about_author: Bram Halloran is the pen name of a former ghostwriter who spent fifteen years putting words in other mouths before claiming a few of his own. He writes love stories from a farmhouse in the Lake District, where the snow is frequent and the letters, he insists, are all sent on time.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In London, Ivo delivers the final chapters of Marguerite Vale's memoirs to her publisher, invisible as ever, and reflects on the decade since he last spoke to her. He almost burns the unsent letter he still keeps. Emotional beat: the ache of a man fluent in everyone's truth but his own.

chapters.title: An Invitation in Winter
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite is summoned to a snowbound inn in the Cotswolds to approve final edits, only to learn her publisher has also invited the mysterious 'consulting editor' — Ivo. Her fury and old longing collide. Emotional beat: the shock of the past arriving with luggage.

chapters.title: Two Roads, One Storm
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both arrive as the storm closes the roads; the inn has one fire, one dining room, and no escape. Their first conversation is all barbed politeness and decade-old subtext. Emotional beat: tension as a duel fought with teacups.

chapters.title: The Manuscript Mistake
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Unable to sleep, Marguerite finds the memoir draft and reads chapters she never wrote — Ivo's ghostwritten account of their twenties, disguised as fiction, including the night they parted. She realizes he has been confessing in code for years. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with tenderness.

chapters.title: What the Snow Erases
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Confronted at dawn, Ivo defends the contract, the confidentiality clause, the professional mask — while the storm knocks out power and forces them to share candles, blankets, and proximity. Emotional beat: duty as a fortress with a cracking wall.

chapters.title: The Night of the Twenties
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Trapped by the storm's worst night, they finally tell each other what really happened ten years ago — her engagement, his silence, the letter he wrote and never sent. Old wounds reopen and, strangely, clean. Emotional beat: grief and relief in the same breath.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The roads clear; the publisher calls demanding the manuscript and threatening legal action over the disguised confession chapters. Ivo must choose: sanitize the truth and keep his career, or deliver the memoir as written and lose everything. Emotional beat: the scales tipping, trembling.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letter
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the inn's last shared breakfast, Ivo chooses truth over duty: he reads the ten-year-old letter aloud, every rehearsed sentence finally spoken. Marguerite answers with the sentence she rehearsed too. Emotional beat: the climax — ten years of silence breaking like ice on a river.

chapters.title: Both Names on the Cover
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Facing the publisher's fury, they negotiate together: Marguerite rewrites the memoir's final chapter as her own letter back to him, and they present it as a co-authored work. Some bridges burn; a better one is built. Emotional beat: love and truth winning, at a price gladly paid.

chapters.title: Spring, First Draft
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Months later, the co-authored book is finished and the unsent letter is framed on Marguerite's wall. Ivo writes under his own name for the first time. Emotional beat: resolution — memory honored, loyalty redefined, and a love finally in the present tense.
